display_name: Howard Park Leston Cabernet Sauvignon, Western Australia
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Margaret River's red gravelly loams force Cabernet Sauvignon roots deep, yielding wines with black currant density and graphite edge. Howard Park Leston blends in Syrah for black pepper lift against the Cab's structure. This 2016 delivers that tension at 14.5% ABV without overripeness.",
  "wine_summary": "Howard Park crafts this Cabernet-dominant blend from Margaret River's western cape vineyards, where the label prioritizes single-vineyard expressions like Leston to highlight site differences. The producer stands out for balancing regional power with restraint, sourcing from ironstone-influenced parcels that build tannic backbone. James Halliday awards it 91 points, signaling consistent quality in a region mimicking Bordeaux's maritime moderation.",
  "terroir_expression": "Red gravelly loam and Forest Grove ironstone soils in Margaret River restrict vigor, concentrating Cabernet's blackberry and cassis while Syrah contributes olive tapenade notes from the iron-rich minerality. The 100km coastal stretch brings cool sea breezes and dry summers, capping alcohol at 14.5% for firm tannins over plush fruit. This geology translates to a savory graphite streak that lingers mid-palate.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested grapes ferment in small batches, then age 18 months in French oak (30% new) to integrate Syrah's rotundone-driven pepper with Cab's structure—rotundone is the sesquiterpene behind black pepper aroma, amplified here without oak dominance. Partial whole-bunch fermentation adds stem-derived spice, preserving the blend's freshness. These choices emphasize site over intervention, yielding pH 3.7 balance in the 2015.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled kangaroo skewers: the wine's black pepper and smoked meat echo the char, while tannins cut gaminess. Nashville hot chicken: Syrah's savory olive counters heat, Cab acidity refreshes spice. Braised beef cheek with parsnips: firm structure matches slow-cooked collagen breakdown, dark fruits meld with root veg earthiness. Seared duck breast: graphite edge slices fat, plum notes pair with fruit reduction.",
  "comparable_wines": "Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet Sauvignon — shares Margaret River gravel structure and black fruit, but less Syrah pepper. Cullen Diana Madeline — similar Cab/Syrah blend with ironstone influence, tighter tannins from biodynamics. Cape Mentelle Cabernet Merlot — regional peer with comparable density, softer from Merlot inclusion.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and peppery savoriness",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2024-2032 for peak integration. Store cool and humid to soften tannins gradually.",
  "value_assessment": "$45-65 retail. Vasse Felix Filius ($50) and Cape Mentelle ($55) compete directly. Buy it—the Syrah edge adds complexity competitors lack at this price.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers list it on steakhouse cards for Australian sections. Retail targets Cabernet fans upgrading from Coonawarra. Collectors track back-vintages like 2015 for TEXSOM bronzes.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you chase Barossa plushness; this demands food to shine. Margaret River purists grab it over Napa Cabs for better acid-tannin frame at half the price. The real win: Syrah coaxes violet lift most tasters miss blind.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 16,

  }
